askCmdr.title: Ask Cmdr

@askCmdr.title.description: Title of the Ask Cmdr chat rail, where the user chats with an AI about their files. This is the product name; keep it as-is.

@askCmdr.close.description: Accessible label for the button that closes the Ask Cmdr chat rail. Sentence case.

@askCmdr.newChat.description: Label for the button that starts a fresh Ask Cmdr conversation. Sentence case.

askCmdr.empty.title: Ask about your files

@askCmdr.empty.title.description: Heading of the Ask Cmdr rail's empty state, shown before the first message. Sentence case.

askCmdr.empty.hint: Cmdr can look at what you’re browsing, your drives, and your file history to answer. It only reads names, paths, and sizes, never file contents.

@askCmdr.empty.hint.description: Explanatory text in the Ask Cmdr rail's empty state, describing what the assistant can see. The apostrophe is a curly typographic apostrophe (U+2019).

@askCmdr.composer.placeholder.description: Placeholder text in the Ask Cmdr message input box. Ends with an ellipsis character (…).

@askCmdr.composer.send.description: Accessible label for the button that sends the typed Ask Cmdr message. Sentence case.

@askCmdr.composer.stop.description: Label for the button that stops the assistant while it is answering. Sentence case.

@askCmdr.thinking.description: Shown while the assistant is reasoning before it starts replying. Ends with an ellipsis character (…).

askCmdr.stalled: This is taking longer than usual. You can keep waiting or stop.

@askCmdr.stalled.description: Ask Cmdr status shown after 30 seconds with no visible assistant text or tool progress. It reassures the user and points to the existing Stop control; avoid the words error and failed.

askCmdr.softCap.message: This chat is getting long. A fresh one keeps replies fast and focused.

@askCmdr.softCap.message.description: A gentle nudge shown once an Ask Cmdr conversation grows past its soft length cap. Friendly, not a hard limit.

@askCmdr.softCap.action.description: Button that starts a new Ask Cmdr conversation, shown alongside the getting-long nudge. Sentence case.

@askCmdr.tool.appState.doing.description: Present-tense status for the assistant reading the user's current view (open folders, cursor, selection). Shown while the tool runs. The apostrophe is U+2019.

askCmdr.tool.appState.done: Looked at what you’re looking at

@askCmdr.tool.appState.done.description: Past-tense label after the assistant read the user's current view. The apostrophe is U+2019.

@askCmdr.tool.listDir.doing.description: Present-tense status for the assistant listing a folder's contents and size. Shown while the tool runs.

@askCmdr.tool.listDir.done.description: Past-tense label after the assistant listed a folder.

@askCmdr.tool.importantFolders.doing.description: Present-tense status for the assistant finding the user's most important folders.

@askCmdr.tool.importantFolders.done.description: Past-tense label after the assistant found the user's most important folders.

@askCmdr.tool.folderImportance.doing.description: Present-tense status for the assistant scoring how important one folder is. The apostrophe is U+2019.

@askCmdr.tool.folderImportance.done.description: Past-tense label after the assistant scored a folder's importance. The apostrophe is U+2019.

@askCmdr.tool.listVolumes.doing.description: Present-tense status for the assistant listing the user's drives and their index freshness.

@askCmdr.tool.listVolumes.done.description: Past-tense label after the assistant listed the user's drives.

@askCmdr.tool.operationsList.doing.description: Present-tense status for the assistant searching the operation log (past copies, moves, deletes, renames).

@askCmdr.tool.operationsList.done.description: Past-tense label after the assistant searched the operation log.

@askCmdr.tool.operationsGet.doing.description: Present-tense status for the assistant reading one logged file operation's detail.

@askCmdr.tool.operationsGet.done.description: Past-tense label after the assistant read one file operation's detail.

@askCmdr.tool.searchPhotos.doing.description: Present-tense status on a tool line in the Ask Cmdr chat rail, shown while the assistant searches the user's photos by description, by text recognized inside them, or by tag. Keep it short: it sits on one line beside a spinner.

@askCmdr.tool.searchPhotos.done.description: Past-tense label on the same tool line once the photo search finished. Pairs with askCmdr.tool.searchPhotos.doing; keep both the same length where the language allows.

@askCmdr.tool.imageFacts.doing.description: Present-tense status on a tool line in the Ask Cmdr chat rail, shown while the assistant reads the text and tags Cmdr recognized inside specific photos the user is looking at (not a search: it already knows which files). This line is a transparency surface, so the wording should make clear that image content is being read. The apostrophe is U+2019.

@askCmdr.tool.imageFacts.done.description: Past-tense label on the same tool line once the assistant finished reading what Cmdr recognized inside those photos. Pairs with askCmdr.tool.imageFacts.doing. The apostrophe is U+2019.

@askCmdr.tool.proposeRenamePlan.doing.description: Present-tense label in the Ask Cmdr chat tool line while it prepares a file rename proposal for the user to review. The tool does not rename anything.

@askCmdr.tool.proposeRenamePlan.done.description: Past-tense label on the Ask Cmdr chat tool line after it prepared a file rename proposal. The user still reviews and approves rows separately. Pairs with askCmdr.tool.proposeRenamePlan.doing.

@askCmdr.tool.listSuggestions.doing.description: Present-tense label on a tool line in the Ask Cmdr chat rail, shown while the assistant looks up the file operations it has already suggested and that are still waiting for the user to approve or reject them. It reads a list, it changes nothing. Pairs with askCmdr.tool.listSuggestions.done.

@askCmdr.tool.listSuggestions.done.description: Past-tense label on the same tool line once the assistant finished looking up its waiting suggestions. Pairs with askCmdr.tool.listSuggestions.doing; keep both the same length where the language allows.

@askCmdr.tool.getSuggestionGroup.doing.description: Present-tense label on a tool line in the Ask Cmdr chat rail, shown while the assistant opens ONE of its suggested groups of file operations to see which files it covers. Reading only. Pairs with askCmdr.tool.getSuggestionGroup.done.

@askCmdr.tool.getSuggestionGroup.done.description: Past-tense label on the same tool line once the assistant finished reading that one suggestion. Pairs with askCmdr.tool.getSuggestionGroup.doing.

@askCmdr.tool.proposeSuggestions.doing.description: Present-tense label on a tool line in the Ask Cmdr chat rail, shown while the assistant prepares file operations (moving, copying, trashing, deleting, renaming, compressing, extracting) for the user to review. Nothing happens to any file: the user decides. Say ''preparing'', never ''doing'' or ''applying''. Pairs with askCmdr.tool.proposeSuggestions.done.

@askCmdr.tool.proposeSuggestions.done.description: Past-tense label on the same tool line once the assistant finished preparing its suggested file operations. The user still reviews and approves each group separately, so this must not read as if anything ran. Pairs with askCmdr.tool.proposeSuggestions.doing.

@askCmdr.tool.nothingToSuggest.doing.description: Present-tense label on a tool line in the Ask Cmdr chat rail, shown while the assistant weighs whether the file activity it was shown is worth telling the person about at all. It is allowed to conclude that nothing is. Nothing is read and nothing changes. The apostrophe is U+2019. Pairs with askCmdr.tool.nothingToSuggest.done.

@askCmdr.tool.nothingToSuggest.done.description: Past-tense label on the same tool line once the assistant decided the activity was not worth raising. It must read as a calm, complete answer rather than as something going wrong: finding nothing is a good outcome. Pairs with askCmdr.tool.nothingToSuggest.doing.

@askCmdr.tool.unknown.doing.description: Present-tense fallback status for a tool the rail doesn't have a specific label for.

@askCmdr.tool.unknown.done.description: Past-tense fallback label for a tool the rail doesn't have a specific label for.

@askCmdr.tool.refused.description: Shown on a tool line when the assistant asked for something Ask Cmdr can't do (it's read-only). The apostrophe is U+2019.

askCmdr.error.noKey: Add your API key in settings to start chatting.

@askCmdr.error.noKey.description: Shown when the chosen AI provider has no API key. Friendly and actionable; avoids the words error and failed.

askCmdr.error.notConfigured: Turn on an AI provider in settings to use Ask Cmdr.

@askCmdr.error.notConfigured.description: Shown when no AI provider is set up. Friendly and actionable; avoids the words error and failed.

askCmdr.error.noConsent: Turn Ask Cmdr on to start chatting. You choose what it can see first.

@askCmdr.error.noConsent.description: Shown when the user hasn't opted into Ask Cmdr yet (or the consent copy changed and needs re-accepting), so the backend refused to send. Friendly and actionable; avoids the words error and failed; points the user at the opt-in screen.

askCmdr.error.localWindowTooSmall: Ask Cmdr needs a bigger context window than your local model has. Pick 16,384 tokens or more in settings, under AI.

@askCmdr.error.localWindowTooSmall.description: Shown in the Ask Cmdr chat when the local AI server is running with a context window too small to hold one message, so Cmdr refused to send rather than have the model reject it. Names the number to pick and where. Friendly and actionable; avoids the words error and failed. Group the number the way the language does. Sentence case.

askCmdr.error.unavailable: Couldn’t reach the AI provider. Check your connection and try again.

@askCmdr.error.unavailable.description: Shown when the AI provider is unreachable. Friendly and actionable; avoids the words error and failed. The apostrophe is U+2019.

askCmdr.error.timeout: That took too long. Try again?

@askCmdr.error.timeout.description: Shown when the AI request timed out. Friendly; avoids the words error and failed.

askCmdr.error.authFailed: The provider didn’t accept your API key. Check it in settings.

@askCmdr.error.authFailed.description: Shown when the provider rejected the API key. Friendly and actionable; avoids the words error and failed. The apostrophe is U+2019.

askCmdr.error.rateLimited: The provider is busy or you’re out of quota. Try again in a bit.

@askCmdr.error.rateLimited.description: Shown when the provider is rate-limiting or the account is out of quota. Friendly; avoids the words error and failed. The apostrophe is U+2019.

askCmdr.error.budgetExhausted: This one hit its limit before finishing. Try asking something more specific.

@askCmdr.error.budgetExhausted.description: Shown when a single answer used up its tool-step or time budget before finishing. Friendly and actionable; avoids the words error and failed.

askCmdr.error.unfinishedReply: The reply didn’t finish. Try again?

@askCmdr.error.unfinishedReply.description: Shown when the reply stream stopped before completing (a provider drop or a crash). Friendly; avoids the words error and failed. The apostrophe is U+2019.

askCmdr.error.provider: Something went wrong on the provider’s side. Try again?

@askCmdr.error.provider.description: Shown for any other provider-side problem. Friendly; avoids the words error and failed. The apostrophe is U+2019.

askCmdr.event.contextTrimmed: Trimmed {count, plural, one {# earlier lookup} other {# earlier lookups}} to fit the model’s context.

@askCmdr.event.contextTrimmed.description: A small centered timeline line in the chat thread, shown when older tool results had to leave the model's context so this turn would fit its token budget. It tells the user the reply was written with less than the whole chat in view. Sentence case. The apostrophe is U+2019.

count.content: How many earlier tool results were left out, as an integer.

@askCmdr.event.modelChanged.description: A small centered timeline line in the chat thread marking that the AI model changed between turns. {model} is the model's technical name, for example openai/gpt-oss-120b.

@askCmdr.loadEarlier.description: Button at the top of a long Ask Cmdr chat that loads the previous page of older messages. Sentence case.

@askCmdr.threads.open.description: Accessible label and tooltip for the rail header button that opens the list of past Ask Cmdr chats. Sentence case.

askCmdr.sessions.title: Chats

@askCmdr.sessions.title.description: Heading of the Ask Cmdr panel listing the user's past chats. Sentence case.

@askCmdr.sessions.back.description: Accessible label for the button that closes the chats list and returns to the active conversation. Sentence case.

@askCmdr.sessions.searchPlaceholder.description: Placeholder in the box that searches across all past Ask Cmdr chats. Ends with an ellipsis character (…).

@askCmdr.sessions.searchLabel.description: Accessible label for the Ask Cmdr chats search input. Sentence case.

@askCmdr.sessions.empty.description: Shown in the chats list when the user has no saved Ask Cmdr conversations. Sentence case.

@askCmdr.sessions.emptyArchived.description: Shown in the chats list, in archived view, when nothing is archived. Sentence case.

@askCmdr.sessions.noResults.description: Shown when a search across past Ask Cmdr chats finds nothing. Sentence case.

@askCmdr.sessions.showArchived.description: Toggle that switches the chats list to show archived conversations. Sentence case.

@askCmdr.sessions.hideArchived.description: Toggle that switches the chats list back to active-only, hiding archived conversations. Sentence case.

@askCmdr.sessions.loadMore.description: Button that loads the next page of older chats in the list. Sentence case.

@askCmdr.sessions.searching.description: Shown while a search across past chats is running. Ends with an ellipsis character (…).

@askCmdr.sessions.rename.description: Accessible label for the button that renames a chat in the list. Sentence case.

@askCmdr.sessions.renameLabel.description: Accessible label for the inline text box that edits a chat's title. Sentence case.

@askCmdr.sessions.archive.description: Accessible label for the button that archives a chat (hides it from the active list, no delete). Sentence case.

@askCmdr.sessions.unarchive.description: Accessible label for the button that restores an archived chat to the active list. Sentence case.

@askCmdr.sessions.archivedBadge.description: Small badge marking an archived chat in the list. Sentence case.

@askCmdr.composer.attach.description: Button in the composer that attaches the file or folder selected in the active pane, so the user can ask about it. Sentence case.

@askCmdr.composer.dropHint.description: Overlay shown on the composer while a file or folder is dragged over it, inviting a drop. Sentence case.

askCmdr.composer.providerOff: Turn on an AI provider in settings to start chatting.

@askCmdr.composer.providerOff.description: Inline hint shown under the Ask Cmdr composer when no AI provider is turned on, so the Send button is disabled. Points the user at settings to turn one on. Friendly and actionable; avoids the words error and failed.

@askCmdr.attachment.remove.description: Accessible label for the small button that removes a staged file or folder attachment from the composer. Sentence case.

askCmdr.consent.title: Talk to Cmdr about your files

@askCmdr.consent.title.description: Heading of the one-time opt-in screen shown before the first Ask Cmdr chat. Warm and inviting. Sentence case.

askCmdr.consent.intro: Ask Cmdr sends your questions to the AI provider you choose, using your own API key. Here’s exactly what leaves your Mac when you chat:

@askCmdr.consent.intro.description: Opening paragraph of the Ask Cmdr consent screen, before the list of what gets sent. Ends with a colon introducing the list. The apostrophe is U+2019.

@askCmdr.consent.item.messages.description: First item in the Ask Cmdr consent list of what leaves the Mac: the text the user types. Short noun phrase, sentence case.

askCmdr.consent.item.names: The names and paths of files and folders Cmdr looks at to answer you

@askCmdr.consent.item.names.description: Consent list item: the file and folder names and paths Cmdr reads to answer. Never the file contents. Sentence case, no period.

@askCmdr.consent.item.sizes.description: Consent list item: the sizes and dates of those files and folders. Short noun phrase, sentence case.

askCmdr.consent.item.envelope: What you’re looking at right now: your current folder, cursor, selection, and connected drives

@askCmdr.consent.item.envelope.description: Consent list item describing the app-state envelope sent with each question: the current folder, cursor position, selection, and connected drives. Sentence case, no period. The apostrophe is U+2019.

askCmdr.consent.item.attachments: Any file or folder you attach to a question, by its name and path only

@askCmdr.consent.item.attachments.description: Consent list item: files or folders the user attaches to a question are sent by reference (name and path), never their contents. Sentence case, no period.

askCmdr.consent.noContents: Cmdr doesn’t send the files themselves: no file contents, no photos, no thumbnails. Photo search is the one thing that reaches inside your images, and only when you have it search them: the text Cmdr recognized inside the matching photos and their tags go to your provider so it can find them. Ask Cmdr only looks and speaks; it never changes anything.

@askCmdr.consent.noContents.description: Reassurance paragraph on the Ask Cmdr consent screen: the files themselves (contents, photos, thumbnails) are never sent; the one exception is photo search, which sends image-derived text (recognized text and tags) when used; and the assistant is read-only. The apostrophes are U+2019.

askCmdr.consent.local: Your chats stay on your Mac, in a local database you can open and read. You pick the provider and model, and you can see what each conversation costs.

@askCmdr.consent.local.description: Paragraph on the Ask Cmdr consent screen: chats are stored locally and the user controls the provider, model, and cost visibility.

askCmdr.consent.logsNote: If you turn on LLM call logging in Advanced settings, Cmdr also saves each request and reply to a folder on your Mac. Those logs stay local too, never sent anywhere.

@askCmdr.consent.logsNote.description: Smaller note on the Ask Cmdr consent screen about the optional local LLM call log (the logLlmCalls setting): the logs are written to a local folder and never transmitted.

@askCmdr.consent.accept.description: Primary button on the Ask Cmdr consent screen that opts in and unlocks the chat. Starts with a verb. Sentence case.

@askCmdr.consent.decline.description: Secondary button on the Ask Cmdr consent screen that closes the rail without opting in. Sentence case.

@askCmdr.cost.tokens.description: The token count in the chat's cost footer. countText is the preformatted number (with thousands separators); count is the raw integer that selects singular or plural.

countText.content: The token count, already formatted with thousands separators, like 1,234.

count.content: The raw token count as an integer, used only to pick the singular or plural word.

@askCmdr.cost.free.description: Cost readout for a chat answered entirely by the local on-device model: it costs nothing. Lowercase, shown after the token count.

@askCmdr.cost.estimate.description: Estimated cost of a chat with a known cloud model. amount is a preformatted currency string like $0.0023. Lowercase 'about' signals it's an estimate, not an exact bill.

amount.content: The estimated cost, already formatted as a currency amount, like $0.0023.

@askCmdr.cost.unknown.description: Cost readout when the chat used a model that isn't in the price table: the tokens are known but the price isn't, so the cost is honestly unknown (never shown as free). Lowercase, shown after the token count.

askCmdr.cost.label: This chat’s usage

@askCmdr.cost.label.description: Accessible label for the chat's cost footer region (token count and estimated cost). The apostrophe is U+2019.

askCmdr.renameReview.title: Review file renames

@askCmdr.renameReview.title.description: Title of the modal where the user reviews an Ask Cmdr rename proposal before files change.

askCmdr.renameReview.description: Cmdr will rename only the files you allow.

@askCmdr.renameReview.description.description: Short explanation under the bulk rename review title. Reassures the user that denied rows will not change.

@askCmdr.renameReview.originalName.description: Column heading for the original file name in the bulk rename review table.

@askCmdr.renameReview.newName.description: Column heading for the proposed file name in the bulk rename review table.

@askCmdr.renameReview.whyThisName.description: Column heading for the rightmost bulk rename review column, which shows what each proposed name is based on.

@askCmdr.renameReview.preview.description: Heading for the narrow thumbnail column in the bulk rename review table. Shown to screen readers only; the column itself is too narrow for a visible label.

@askCmdr.renameReview.openPreview.description: Accessible name of the per-row thumbnail button in the bulk rename review, which opens the file in the viewer so the user can check the proposed name against the file itself.

askCmdr.renameReview.openPreviewTooltip: Open the file to check the name (Space)

@askCmdr.renameReview.openPreviewTooltip.description: Tooltip on the per-row thumbnail button in the bulk rename review. Names the keyboard shortcut that opens the focused row's file.

@askCmdr.renameReview.editName.description: Accessible label for the editable new name field in each bulk rename review row, so a wrong proposed name can be corrected in place instead of denied. Placeholder is the file's current name.

askCmdr.renameReview.nameRejected: Cmdr can’t use that name. Try a different one.

@askCmdr.renameReview.nameRejected.description: Per-row message shown when the name the user typed in the bulk rename review is not a usable filename, so the row went back to the name it had. Conversational and actionable; never the words error or failed. The apostrophe is a curly typographic apostrophe (U+2019).

@askCmdr.renameReview.evidence.imageText.description: Label above a quote of the text Cmdr recognized inside the image, shown as the reason for a proposed name.

askCmdr.renameReview.evidence.imageTags: What Cmdr sees in the image

@askCmdr.renameReview.evidence.imageTags.description: Label above the image tags Cmdr recognized, shown as the reason for a proposed name.

@askCmdr.renameReview.evidence.filename.description: Label shown when a proposed name comes from the file's existing name, with nothing read from inside the file.

@askCmdr.renameReview.evidence.metadata.description: Label shown when a proposed name comes only from metadata like the date or size. It must read as an honest limit: nothing inside the file was read.

@askCmdr.renameReview.evidence.userInstr.description: Label shown when a proposed name follows a naming rule the user stated in the chat.

@askCmdr.renameReview.evidence.userEdite.description: Label shown in the bulk rename review when the user replaced the proposed name with one they typed themselves. The row then carries no evidence at all, and never the model’s.

@askCmdr.renameReview.coverage.description: Caption under the quote in the bulk rename review's evidence column, saying how much of the text Cmdr read in the image the quote covers. Lets the user see that a short match inside a page of recognized text is weak evidence for a name. Both numbers arrive preformatted with thousands separators.

matchedText.content: How many characters the quote covers, preformatted.

totalText.content: How many characters Cmdr read in the image, preformatted.

askCmdr.renameReview.coverageThin: That’s a small part of the text Cmdr read here. Open the file to check the name.

@askCmdr.renameReview.coverageThin.description: Tooltip and accessible label on the warning marker beside a thin coverage figure in the bulk rename review. Tells the user the quote covers only a sliver of the recognized text, so the name deserves a look at the file itself. Never says the name is wrong: Cmdr cannot know that. The apostrophe is a curly typographic apostrophe (U+2019).

@askCmdr.renameReview.allow.description: Button that lets one proposed file rename proceed.

@askCmdr.renameReview.deny.description: Button that prevents one proposed file rename from proceeding.

@askCmdr.renameReview.allowAll.description: Button that allows every currently reviewable rename in the proposal.

@askCmdr.renameReview.denyAll.description: Button that denies every rename in the proposal.

@askCmdr.renameReview.cancel.description: Button that closes the bulk rename review and discards its proposal without renaming files.

askCmdr.renameReview.rename: Rename {count, plural, one {# file} other {# files}}

@askCmdr.renameReview.rename.description: Disabled-until-apply primary action label in the bulk rename review. count is the number of allowed rows.

count.content: The number of allowed rename rows.

askCmdr.renameReview.blocked: This rename needs attention before it can continue.

@askCmdr.renameReview.blocked.description: Generic per-row message when backend preflight blocks a proposed rename.

@askCmdr.renameReview.overwriteBadge.description: Compact red warning badge beside a proposed filename when another file already occupies that name. Keep the parentheses and exclamation mark.

askCmdr.renameReview.overwriteTooltip: Another file already uses this name and isn''t part of this rename plan. This rename is blocked to protect it.

@askCmdr.renameReview.overwriteTooltip.description: Accessible tooltip for the overwrite warning badge. Explains that the existing file is outside the rename plan and will not be replaced.

@askCmdr.renameReview.sourceMissingBadge.description: Compact red warning badge beside a bulk rename row whose proposed source file does not exist. Keep the parentheses.

askCmdr.renameReview.sourceMissingToolti: This source file no longer exists. It may have been deleted or renamed outside Cmdr.

@askCmdr.renameReview.sourceMissingToolt.description: Accessible tooltip for the missing-source warning badge. Explains that the row is blocked because its original file is gone.

@askCmdr.renameReview.extensionBadge.description: Compact yellow warning badge beside a proposed filename when the rename changes, adds, or removes its filename extension. Keep the parentheses.

askCmdr.renameReview.extensionTooltip: Extension changed. The file contents will not be converted.

@askCmdr.renameReview.extensionTooltip.description: Accessible tooltip for the extension-change warning badge in the bulk rename review. Explains that renaming an extension does not convert the file format.

@askCmdr.renameReview.cycleBadge.description: Compact yellow warning badge beside each proposed rename that belongs to a dependency cycle. Keep the parentheses.

askCmdr.renameReview.cycleTooltip: Rename cycle. Cmdr will use one temporary name while rotating these files.

@askCmdr.renameReview.cycleTooltip.description: Accessible tooltip for the rename-cycle warning badge. Explains that Cmdr needs one temporary filename to rotate the files safely.

@askCmdr.renameReview.nothingReadBadge.description: Compact badge beside a proposed filename in the bulk rename review when Cmdr read nothing inside the file, so the name rests on the old name, the file details, or the user’s instruction. Keep the parentheses.

askCmdr.renameReview.nothingReadTooltip: Cmdr read nothing inside this file. This name comes from the old name, the file’s details, or what you asked for.

@askCmdr.renameReview.nothingReadTooltip.description: Accessible tooltip for the nothing-read badge in the bulk rename review. It must stay an honest limit: nothing inside the file was read. Never soften it into something reassuring. The apostrophe is a curly typographic apostrophe (U+2019).

@askCmdr.renameReview.nameKeptBadge.description: Compact badge beside a proposed filename in the bulk rename review when Cmdr kept the file’s current name because it read nothing inside the file. Keep the parentheses.

askCmdr.renameReview.nameKeptTooltip: Cmdr kept the current name and read nothing inside this file.

@askCmdr.renameReview.nameKeptTooltip.description: Accessible tooltip for the name-kept badge in the bulk rename review. Says both halves plainly: the name did not change, and nothing inside the file was read. Never soften it.

askCmdr.renameReview.expired: This review expired. Ask Cmdr to prepare it again.

@askCmdr.renameReview.expired.description: Message when the server-side rename proposal is no longer reviewable, because it was already applied, turned down, or replaced.

askCmdr.renameReview.status: {allowed, plural, one {# rename allowed} other {# renames allowed}}; {blocked, plural, one {# blocked} other {# blocked}}

@askCmdr.renameReview.status.description: Screen-reader status summary for the bulk rename review list. allowed and blocked are raw counts.

allowed.content: The number of currently allowed rows.

blocked.content: The number of rows blocked by preflight.

@askCmdr.renameUndo.applied.description: A line in the Ask Cmdr chat thread, shown right after a batch of files was renamed. It reports what happened and sits beside an Undo button. Sentence case.

countText.content: How many files were renamed, ready to drop into the sentence (e.g. 1,234).

count.content: The same number of files (decides whether the noun is singular or plural).

@askCmdr.renameUndo.undo.description: Button beside the 'Renamed N files.' line in the Ask Cmdr chat thread. Puts the files' previous names back. Keep it short: it sits inline in a narrow side panel.

@askCmdr.renameUndo.undoLabel.description: Accessible name (aria-label) for the Undo button beside the 'Renamed N files.' line, so a screen reader announces WHAT would be undone rather than a bare 'Undo'. Never shown on screen.

countText.content: How many files this button would rename back, ready to drop into the sentence (e.g. 1,234).

count.content: The same number of files (decides whether the noun is singular or plural).

@askCmdr.renameUndo.undoJob.description: Second button, shown only when the user renamed files in several batches during one run: it undoes every batch at once. A 'batch' is one reviewed group of renames the user approved. Keep it short: it sits inline in a narrow side panel.

countText.content: How many batches would be undone, ready to drop into the sentence (e.g. 12).

count.content: The same number of batches (decides whether the noun is singular or plural).

askCmdr.renameUndo.undoJobLabel: Undo every rename in this run: {filesText} {files, plural, one {file} other {files}} across {batches, plural, one {# batch} other {# batches}}

@askCmdr.renameUndo.undoJobLabel.description: Accessible name (aria-label) for the 'Undo all N batches' button, naming both totals so a screen reader conveys the scale of what would be undone. A 'batch' is one reviewed group of renames the user approved. Never shown on screen.

filesText.content: Total files across every batch, ready to drop into the sentence (e.g. 1,234).

files.content: The same number of files (decides whether the noun is singular or plural).

batches.content: How many batches would be undone.

@askCmdr.renameUndo.undoing.description: Replaces the Undo button while the undo is running. Renaming files back can take a moment on a network drive, so this is a progress state, not a result. Sentence case; the character at the end is an ellipsis (U+2026).

@askCmdr.renameUndo.undone.description: Result line shown when an undo put every file's previous name back. Sentence case.

countText.content: How many files got their previous name back, ready to drop into the sentence (e.g. 1,234).

count.content: The same number of files (decides whether the noun is singular or plural).

@askCmdr.renameUndo.partial.description: First of two lines shown when an undo could only put SOME files back; the second line is askCmdr.renameUndo.skipped. Same wording as askCmdr.renameUndo.undone, kept as its own key because it is followed by the explanation line and translators may want to pair the two. Sentence case.

countText.content: How many files got their previous name back, ready to drop into the sentence (e.g. 1,234).

count.content: The same number of files (decides whether the noun is singular or plural).

askCmdr.renameUndo.skipped: Left {countText} {count, plural, one {file} other {files}} alone: {count, plural, one {it changed} other {they changed}} since the rename, or the old name is taken again.

@askCmdr.renameUndo.skipped.description: Second line of a partial undo result: it explains why some files kept their new names. Cmdr never overwrites during an undo, so a file that changed after the rename, or whose old name now belongs to something else, is deliberately left as it is. Say this as a considered choice, not as something going wrong. Sentence case.

countText.content: How many files were left as they are, ready to drop into the sentence (e.g. 1,234).

count.content: The same number of files (decides whether the noun is singular or plural).

askCmdr.renameUndo.skipReason.drift.name: Left {name} alone: it changed since the rename.

@askCmdr.renameUndo.skipReason.drift.nam.description: One line of a partial undo result in the Ask Cmdr chat thread, saying which of the renamed files kept their new names and why. This version is used when the reason applies to exactly ONE file, so the line names it. This reason: the file was edited after Cmdr renamed it, so putting the old name back would touch a file the user has since changed. Cmdr never overwrites while undoing, so say this as a considered choice, not as something going wrong. Sentence case.

name.content: The file’s own name, e.g. invoice-2026.pdf. Never translate it: it is the real name on disk.

askCmdr.renameUndo.skipReason.drift.coun: Left {countText} {count, plural, one {file} other {files}} alone: they changed since the rename.

@askCmdr.renameUndo.skipReason.drift.cou.description: One line of a partial undo result in the Ask Cmdr chat thread, saying which of the renamed files kept their new names and why. This version is used when the reason applies to two or more files, so the line counts them instead of naming them. This reason: the file was edited after Cmdr renamed it, so putting the old name back would touch a file the user has since changed. Cmdr never overwrites while undoing, so say this as a considered choice, not as something going wrong. Sentence case.

countText.content: How many files this reason applies to, ready to drop into the sentence (e.g. 1,234). Always two or more.

count.content: The same number of files (decides whether the noun is singular or plural).

Left {name} alone: its old name is taken again.

@askCmdr.renameUndo.skipReason.nameTaken.description: One line of a partial undo result in the Ask Cmdr chat thread, saying which of the renamed files kept their new names and why. This version is used when the reason applies to exactly ONE file, so the line names it. This reason: something else now sits at the name the file used to have, so the file keeps its new name. Cmdr never overwrites while undoing, so say this as a considered choice, not as something going wrong. Sentence case.

name.content: The file’s own name, e.g. invoice-2026.pdf. Never translate it: it is the real name on disk.

Left {countText} {count, plural, one {file} other {files}} alone: their old names are taken again.

@askCmdr.renameUndo.skipReason.nameTaken.description: One line of a partial undo result in the Ask Cmdr chat thread, saying which of the renamed files kept their new names and why. This version is used when the reason applies to two or more files, so the line counts them instead of naming them. This reason: something else now sits at the name the file used to have, so the file keeps its new name. Cmdr never overwrites while undoing, so say this as a considered choice, not as something going wrong. Sentence case.

countText.content: How many files this reason applies to, ready to drop into the sentence (e.g. 1,234). Always two or more.

count.content: The same number of files (decides whether the noun is singular or plural).

askCmdr.renameUndo.skipReason.unverifiab: Left {name} alone: Cmdr couldn’t check whether it changed.

@askCmdr.renameUndo.skipReason.unverifia.description: One line of a partial undo result in the Ask Cmdr chat thread, saying which of the renamed files kept their new names and why. This version is used when the reason applies to exactly ONE file, so the line names it. This reason: the drive could not tell Cmdr whether the file has changed since the rename (some network drives and phones cannot), and Cmdr never renames a file it cannot check first. Say this as caution, not as a fault. Sentence case; the apostrophe is U+2019.

name.content: The file’s own name, e.g. invoice-2026.pdf. Never translate it: it is the real name on disk.

askCmdr.renameUndo.skipReason.unverifiab: Left {countText} {count, plural, one {file} other {files}} alone: Cmdr couldn’t check whether they changed.

@askCmdr.renameUndo.skipReason.unverifia.description: One line of a partial undo result in the Ask Cmdr chat thread, saying which of the renamed files kept their new names and why. This version is used when the reason applies to two or more files, so the line counts them instead of naming them. This reason: the drive could not tell Cmdr whether the file has changed since the rename (some network drives and phones cannot), and Cmdr never renames a file it cannot check first. Say this as caution, not as a fault. Sentence case; the apostrophe is U+2019.

countText.content: How many files this reason applies to, ready to drop into the sentence (e.g. 1,234). Always two or more.

count.content: The same number of files (decides whether the noun is singular or plural).

askCmdr.renameUndo.skipReason.folderNotE: Left the folder {name} alone: it has something in it now.

@askCmdr.renameUndo.skipReason.folderNot.description: One line of a partial undo result, about FOLDERS rather than files. This reason: undoing would have removed a folder Cmdr created, but something has been put inside it since, so Cmdr keeps the folder and what is in it. This version is used when the reason applies to exactly ONE file, so the line names it. Cmdr never overwrites while undoing, so say this as a considered choice, not as something going wrong. Sentence case.

name.content: The folder’s own name, e.g. Scans. Never translate it: it is the real name on disk.

askCmdr.renameUndo.skipReason.folderNotE: Left {countText} {count, plural, one {folder} other {folders}} alone: they have something in them now.

@askCmdr.renameUndo.skipReason.folderNot.description: One line of a partial undo result, about FOLDERS rather than files. This reason: undoing would have removed a folder Cmdr created, but something has been put inside it since, so Cmdr keeps the folder and what is in it. This version is used when the reason applies to two or more files, so the line counts them instead of naming them. Cmdr never overwrites while undoing, so say this as a considered choice, not as something going wrong. Sentence case.

countText.content: How many folders this reason applies to, ready to drop into the sentence (e.g. 1,234). Always two or more.

count.content: The same number of folders (decides whether the noun is singular or plural).

askCmdr.renameUndo.skipReason.failed.nam: Left {name} alone: Cmdr couldn’t put its old name back.

@askCmdr.renameUndo.skipReason.failed.na.description: One line of a partial undo result in the Ask Cmdr chat thread, saying which of the renamed files kept their new names and why. This version is used when the reason applies to exactly ONE file, so the line names it. This reason: the drive refused to rename the file back (it is disconnected, read-only, or reported a problem). Unlike the other reasons this one is not a deliberate choice, so it may be worth trying again. Sentence case; the apostrophe is U+2019.

name.content: The file’s own name, e.g. invoice-2026.pdf. Never translate it: it is the real name on disk.

askCmdr.renameUndo.skipReason.failed.cou: Left {countText} {count, plural, one {file} other {files}} alone: Cmdr couldn’t put their old names back.

@askCmdr.renameUndo.skipReason.failed.co.description: One line of a partial undo result in the Ask Cmdr chat thread, saying which of the renamed files kept their new names and why. This version is used when the reason applies to two or more files, so the line counts them instead of naming them. This reason: the drive refused to rename the file back (it is disconnected, read-only, or reported a problem). Unlike the other reasons this one is not a deliberate choice, so it may be worth trying again. Sentence case; the apostrophe is U+2019.

countText.content: How many files this reason applies to, ready to drop into the sentence (e.g. 1,234). Always two or more.

count.content: The same number of files (decides whether the noun is singular or plural).

askCmdr.renameUndo.refusedBatches: Cmdr couldn’t undo {countText} {count, plural, one {batch} other {batches}}. The operation log has the details.

@askCmdr.renameUndo.refusedBatches.description: Extra line of a partial undo result, shown when whole batches could not be reversed at all (already undone, or a drive they need is disconnected). 'The operation log' is Cmdr's history of file changes; use whatever your locale calls that feature. A 'batch' is one reviewed group of renames the user approved. Sentence case; the apostrophe is U+2019.

countText.content: How many batches could not be undone, ready to drop into the sentence (e.g. 3).

count.content: The same number of batches (decides whether the noun is singular or plural).

askCmdr.renameUndo.unavailable: Nothing to put back. This batch may already be undone, or its drive isn’t connected.

@askCmdr.renameUndo.unavailable.description: Result line shown when an undo reversed nothing at all: the batch had already been undone, or a drive it needs is not connected. Says what is true without guessing which of the two it was. Sentence case; the apostrophe is U+2019.

askCmdr.context.label: How full this chat is

@askCmdr.context.label.description: Accessible label for the chat's context-usage gauge in the rail footer.

@askCmdr.context.tooltip.description: Tooltip on the context-usage gauge. usedText and budgetText are preformatted numbers (with thousands separators). Both are chars/4 estimates, never a tokenizer's count, so the copy says so.

askCmdr.wake.thinking: Ask Cmdr is having a look at what changed. Open the chat.

@askCmdr.wake.thinking.description: Tooltip and spoken label on the status-corner indicator shown while Ask Cmdr is running a conversation it started on its own. Pressing it opens that chat in the rail, which is what the second sentence promises. Sentence case; two short sentences, because the label has to say both what is happening and what pressing it does.

askCmdr.wake.stop: Stop what Ask Cmdr is doing

@askCmdr.wake.stop.description: Spoken label and tooltip on the small stop button beside that indicator, which ends the conversation Ask Cmdr started on its own. Longer than the rail's bare "Stop" on purpose: this button carries no visible text and sits in the window corner, so the label is the only thing naming what it stops. Sentence case, no full stop.

askCmdr.wake.needsFullDiskAccess: Ask Cmdr can only watch folders it can see. Set up full disk access.

@askCmdr.wake.needsFullDiskAccess.description: Tooltip and spoken label on the status-corner indicator shown when the user let Ask Cmdr watch their folders but macOS Full Disk Access is still outstanding, so the agent can only see part of the disk. Pressing it opens the system privacy settings. Only ever shown to somebody who opted in, so it reads as a step left to finish, never as a warning. The second sentence names Apple's own setting: use the same wording as `search.coverage.setUpFullDiskAccess` so the two surfaces agree. Sentence case.

askCmdr.wake.needsApiKey: Ask Cmdr is watching, but it needs an API key to think. Open settings.

@askCmdr.wake.needsApiKey.description: Tooltip and spoken label on the status-corner indicator shown when the user let Ask Cmdr watch their folders but no AI provider is configured, so nothing can be sent anywhere. Pressing it opens Cmdr's AI settings. "Ask Cmdr" is the feature name and stays untranslated. Sentence case.
